rule.description: A group of data values that repeatedly travels together through the resolution, nested-validation and test-dispatch pipeline but is declared and handed over as unrelated individual parameters. The rule records every function-like signature and every bare positional parameter hand-off from src/**/*.ts via a case-specific ESLint rule, then a cross-file aggregation reports (a) identical parameter-name groups recurring across multiple signatures (3-4 names recurring in >=5 signatures across >=4 files, larger groups in >=2 signatures across >=2 files, maximal groups only) and (b) parameter groups handed over as an unbroken run of >=3 bare positional arguments at >=4 call sites across >=3 files. The hand-off relation is structural, so uniform renames do not dissolve it.

checks.description: The resolve-context data (the value being resolved, its parent object, and the shared validation context) is re-declared as separate positional parameters at each resolution seam it reaches.
checks.detected_relation: signature -> re-declared {value, parent, context} parameter-position membership (group recurs in 6 signatures across 4 files)
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: These three values form one resolution context; repeating them as loose parameters at every seam is the data clump this case studies, where a single named parameter object would carry the context.

matches.evidence: Reference#getValue(value, parent, context) declares the resolve context positionally at the anchor seam that all other injected trio signatures mirror.
Reference#cast re-declares the trio positionally instead of accepting the existing cast options object.
ObjectSchema#_getDefault(value, parent, context) re-threads the context positionally into per-field default derivation.
Schema#_getDefault(value, parent, context) re-declares the context that default thunks already consume as an object.
resolveParams(params, value, parent, context) resolves message parameters by re-threading the context positionally.
resolveMaybeRef(item, value, parent, context) unwraps refs against the positional trio.

checks.description: The validation test-run context (value, path, options, originalValue, schema plus the panic/next callbacks) is re-declared as separate positional parameters across the test-kit contract and its dispatch sites, and the {options, panic, next} portion recurs across the queued-test dispatch as well as the pre-existing collection-schema dispatch.
checks.detected_relation: signature -> re-declared test-run context parameter-position membership (7-name group in 3 signatures; 6-name maximal group in 4 signatures; {options, panic, next} in 8 signatures across 5 files; {panic, next, _value} in 5 signatures across 4 files)
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The queued-test invocation carries one execution context that is instead expanded into positional slots at every protocol declaration and dispatch site; the clump also crosses into the collection-schema validators whose own dispatch signatures share the same loose {options, panic, next} thread.

matches.evidence: The RunTest contract re-declares the whole test-run context (value, path, options, originalValue, schema, panic, next) positionally.
The Test contract mirrors the same positional test-run context (value, path, options, originalValue, schema, panic, next).
validate(value, path, options, originalValue, schema, panic, next) implements the contract by taking the whole run context as loose parameters.
RunTest also belongs to the maximal 6-name group {next, options, originalValue, panic, path, value} shared with the dispatch method.
Schema#runTests(tests, value, originalValue, path, options, panic, next) positionally dispatches the queued tests it is handed.
Test belongs to the maximal 6-name protocol group shared with Schema#runTests.
validate belongs to the maximal 6-name protocol group shared with Schema#runTests.
ArraySchema#_validate declares the loose {options, panic, next} dispatch thread that the injected protocol signatures join into a recurrent group of 8 signatures.
ObjectSchema#_validate declares the same loose {options, panic, next} dispatch thread.
Schema#_validate declares the same loose {options, panic, next} dispatch thread.
TupleSchema#_validate declares the same loose {options, panic, next} dispatch thread.
RunTest carries {options, panic, next} as loose trailing parameters, joining the collection dispatch signatures into one recurrent group.
Test carries the same loose {options, panic, next} trailing parameters.
validate declares the protocol values plus the same loose {options, panic, next} trailing parameters.
Schema#runTests declares {options, panic, next} alongside the queued tests, re-typing the dispatch thread at the runner seam.
ArraySchema#_validate keeps {_value, panic, next} loose, which the injected nested-test arrow (declaring _value/_originalValue-style slots) grows into a recurrent 5-signature group.
ObjectSchema#_validate keeps {_value, panic, next} loose, part of the same recurrent group.
Schema#_validate keeps {_value, panic, next} loose, part of the same recurrent group.
TupleSchema#_validate keeps {_value, panic, next} loose, part of the same recurrent group.
The nested-test factory returned by Schema#asNestedTest re-declares the entire positional protocol (value, path, options, originalValue, schema, panic, next) for every field/item test closure.

checks.description: The nested-validation site descriptor (the field key or entry index, the parent value, the parent path, the original pre-cast parent, and the options) is re-declared as six separate positional parameters.
checks.detected_relation: signature -> re-declared {key, index, parent, parentPath, originalParent, options} parameter-position membership (group recurs in 3 signatures across 3 files, including the interface contract)
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: One nested-site descriptor is expanded into position slots on the base schema, the lazy schema and the ISchema contract, so every participating schema type must repeat a fixed positional order.

matches.evidence: Schema#asNestedTest declares (key, index, parent, parentPath, originalParent, options) as loose positionals that every nesting site must thread.
Lazy#asNestedTest re-declares the same six positional slots to forward the nested-site context to the resolved schema.
The ISchema interface contract was widened to the same six positional parameters, so every schema implementation must mirror the positional order.

checks.description: The resolve-context trio is handed over as an unbroken run of bare positional arguments inside single calls, rather than being carried by a named object.
checks.detected_relation: call-site -> bare positional run of >=3 signature formals forwarded together (group {value, parent, context} forwarded at 4 sites across 3 files)
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The values travel together through consecutive hand-offs in exactly the positional order of their declarations, which is the movement pattern of an unencapsulated data clump; the relation is structural, so uniform renames do not remove it.

matches.evidence: Reference#cast forwards (value, parent, context) as three bare arguments to getValue.
ObjectSchema#_getDefault forwards (value, parent, context) as three bare arguments to the superclass _getDefault.
resolveParams forwards (value, parent, context) as three bare arguments to resolveMaybeRef.
resolveMaybeRef forwards (value, parent, context) as three bare arguments to Reference#getValue.

excluded: Destructured single-object parameters (a signature that accepts one options/config object and destructures it) do not count as clump members; only identifier parameters are recorded.
Rest parameters, computed keys and pattern parameters carry no clump member name and are skipped.

Lone delegation sites that forward the same positional protocol to the same operation (wrapper methods such as the Lazy validateAt/validateSyncAt re-entry, the collection-schema super._validate calls, the ValidationError constructor chain, or util helpers like reach/getIn) stay below the >=4 sites across >=3 files recurrence threshold and are not reported.
Groups fully contained in a larger qualifying recurrent group (larger name set and superset signature set) are not reported twice.
Callback/deferred functions in test-suite code are not scanned; only src/**/*.ts is analyzed.
